recipes.name: Whole Wheat Cereal Bars
ingredients_raw: 3 cups coarsely chopped shredded whole wheat cereal biscuits

steps.text: Combine brown sugar, honey, and peanut butter in a microwave-safe glass or ceramic bowl. Melt the peanut butter mixture microwave in 30 second intervals, stirring after each melting, for 1 to 2 minutes (depending on your microwave). Stir in cereal and raisins.
Press cereal mixture into an 8 inch square pan sprayed with non-stick spray. Cool and cut into bars.

raw_recipe.headline: Whole Wheat Cereal Bars
raw_recipe.description: Whole wheat cereal biscuits are mixed with honey, peanut butter and raisins for this delicious bar.

review.reviewBody: Great way to use up the shredded wheat and have a little something sweet too. I added 1 additional cup of cereal for a total of 4 cups, did not pack the brown sugar, added 1 teaspoon of vanilla and replaced raisins with semi-sweet mini chocolate chips sprinkled on top. For the stove top method, I brought the brown sugar and honey to a boil, removed from heat, added peanut butter and vanilla, stirred until smooth, poured over cereal, mixed, poured into pan, sprinkled with chocolate chips. Yum!

These were so yummy- - I did the stovetop method and as another viewer suggested did not pack the sugar, added 1 tsp of vanilla and sprinkled mini chocolate chips on top. Imagine my surprise when my anti- shredded wheat husband-( I told him it would be like a Triscuit) and chocolate loving husband said he thought it would also be good with raisins! I added one cup extra shredded wheat.

Delicous. I did have to cook it on the stove to get it set into bars though, the microwave did not work for me. I brought the brown sugar, honey (which can be replaced with corn syrup if need be) and peanut butter just to a boil in a small pan on the stove, stirring often, and then dumped over the ceral and raisins in a mixing bowl. My favourite is to use special k.

I’ve made this 4 times now. The first 3 I used fresh cranberries because I had a bunch of them. Tonight I made it with NSA tart cherries. I've added unsweet coconut to each batch because I love it! (I cook the way I'd want it if i could eat it.) Coconut so good for you! I’ve had plain wheat cereal and frosted wheat cereal. I don’t eat sugar added things or gluten & husband is pre-diabetic so I used 2 c unsweetened cereal with 1 c sweeten in order to get rid of it. (These cereals were gifted to us by a friend.) Husband has really enjoyed the cranberry ones & have left the cherry added ones for him to see in the morning when he’s getting his lunch together. (Our shifts don’t coincide right now.) Side note… One night when we were watching a movie I crushed 2 boxes of unsweetened wheat squares and one box of the sweetened variety and placed in labeled ziplocks with the proper measurement. (It took the entire movie but what else are you going to do? lol) I highly recommend, if you have time, to pre-crush the entire box(es) because it’s wonderful to have that ready to toss in the bowl. While this recipe is super easy this step is a huge time saver and throws together so much faster! These will last quite a while in the fridge but husband ate 1-2 bars a day and they didn’t last long. We’re older so no kids/grandkids in the house full time and they still went fast! I will admit that we went to see our son and grand daughter (she is very picky!) and she loved these too and we ended up leaving the rest of that batch with them to devour. Try it and add different ingredients… unsweetened peanut butter, both cereals, unsweet coconut, cacao nibs, or different unsweet fruits… it won't disappoint! Thank you for the recipe… It's a keeper! for us!

I made this because I was given a box of shredded wheat & no one was eating it. So before it expired I came on this site & looked up ideas of what to do with it so it would be eaten. 
I made alot of changes to this. I basically kept all the ingredients the same but instead of using raisins cause no one likes them, I used cranberries (Ocean Spray), added more peanut butter & honey. I kept it covered in the pan overnight & put it on a cake board then used chocolate raspberry sauce drizzled over top. I then cut it into bite size pieces. Everyone loved them! The kids didn't suspect a thing (17&3 yrs) 
I'm sure u can more or less of anything, but I'll be definitely be making this again & probably change up the ingrediants :)
5 Stars from me!

I decided to press the mixture into a muffin tin instead of a square dish because it eliminated the need to cut the bars (and dirty another knife). The mixture was super sticky so I had to dust my fingers with flour in order to do any pressing. I will make this again too, mayb with nutella instead of peanut butter!

Boiling instead of microwaving definitely makes the difference in this recipe. The mixture came out a clay-like consistency, and I packed them into a mini-muffin tray to make bit sized cereal bars! If you decide to use chocolate chips like I did, be sure to mix them in at the very end or they'll melt and stick to the spoon.
I just made a review but forgot to say I omitted raisons and used choc chips (half milk half semisweet) :)
these are delicious! REALLY sweet, but...i like sweet :) definitely don't pack the brown sugar! i made these with a stale box of rice krispies and it worked wonderfully.

I needed to use up some Shredded Wheat cereal that no-one was eating so this recipe was perfect! because of my changes I felt I should only give 4 stars. I didn't have any honey so i took my 1/2 measurer and filled it almost all the way with light corn syrup, then the rest of the way with a few T of maple syrup for flavor. The cereal gave a nice crunch , the raisins made them a bit chewy and the peanut flavor was mild imo... I had trouble trying to cut them into bars since they were a bit soft and gooey; maybe the honey would have made them firmer! I may add some chopped peanuts next time as well! Thanks for the recipe. :)

So delicious!
I substituted smooth for chunky peanut butter.
This was super easy to make and tasted so good. I didn’t have any sugar so omitted that completely and they were great. I will definitely make them again.

This tasted pretty good and was a nice way to use up shredded wheat. I added 4 cups of shredded wheat instead of 3 in order to use up 2 full pouches. The bars were pretty messy to eat and never really set up, which wasn't too bad since that means it stayed soft but don't expect a granola bar consistency. It's not exactly healthy either. You could add most anything to it and it would be good: chocolate chips, nuts, cranberries, cheerios...

I made this exactly as written and just got sweet goop, even after leaving it in the fridge for an hour. The taste was fine, if heavy on the honey, but what a waste of sugar. The reason shredded wheat goes uneaten is that it's unsweetened. I wish I'd just added sweetener to a bowl of cereal instead. It would've meant eating much less sugar overall and enjoying the cereal more.
